newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Future of Sweden's Orrefors to be clear next week.
newsitem.headline: Future of Sweden's Orrefors to be clear next week.

text.p: The future of Swedish glassmaker Orrefors Kosta Boda AB will be made crystal clear next week after weeks of uncertainty with the company's three main owners locked in talks over future ownership.
A joint statement on Friday said Swedish investment groups Investor AB and Proventus AB and Danish porcelain and silver group Royal Copenhagen AS, were in discussions.
Trading in Orrefors Kosta Boda was suspended, with last trade at 140 crowns, pending an announcement expected Tuesday at the latest.
"The parties have agreed that they will not comment before everything is settled," Investor spokesman Nils Ingvar Lundin told Reuters.

Investor, the investment arm of Sweden's Wallenberg business empire, is the largest shareholder of the glassmaker which was formed in 1990 by the merger of rivals Orrefors and Kosta Boda. The two prestigious trademarks remain separate.
A fight over the ownership of the glassmaker broke out earlier this month between Royal Copenhagen and Proventus.
"But no-one yet knows where Investor, with a 23.1 percent holding, stands," said one Swedish market analyst.
The battle began when Royal Copenhagen, which is 82 percent owned by Danish brewer Carlsberg AS, raised its holding in the glass company to 17.1 percent.
It said this was a sign of good faith, building on a sales alliance agreed between Royal Copenhagen and Orrefors Kosta Boda in July.
But the move prompted Proventus to seek to raise its own stake in Orrefors, warning that it suspected Royal Copenhagen of trying to bring the prestigious label under Danish control.
Proventus lifted its stake in the top quality glassmaker to 21.1 percent of capital and votes and bought an option that would allow it take a further 9.1 percent stake.
Proventus then bid 145 crowns a share to shareholders in Orrefors for shares corresponding to 20 percent of the capital in the company.

Concerns that the Danish luxury goods maker was eyeing a possible takeover raised fears amongst designers at Orrefors Kosta Bodda who told Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter that they did not want to work for a Danish company.
Orrefors and Kosta Boda are considered two of the country's most prestigious products, widely bought by overseas tourists and a great source of pride to Sweden.
Unlisted Proventus is owned 91.5 percent by Swedish financier Robert Weil and 8.5 percent by the company's managing director Mikael Kamras.
Orrefors Kosta Boda on Friday reported a profit after financial items of 20.6 million crowns ($3.1 million) for the first nine months of 1996 compared to 30.9 million a year ago.
Sales sank to 461.5 million crowns from 489.6 million.
